subject: Acceptance gatebackfill and escalation: MAP v2 proposal
messages:
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Miles <j.miles@acmehealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acceptance gatebackfill and escalation: MAP v2 proposal

Jordan / Acme procurement — thanks again for the candid update this morning. Based on our call, we put together a focused revision to the MAP that explicitly accounts for the acceptance gate backlog you called out and the downstream impact on the close date. Attached: MAP-v2.xlsx (changes highlighted) and a short diagram that shows the new gating windows.

Key points up front: 
- Proposed new acceptance window: 2026-10-04 to 2026-10-11 (moves final acceptance by 10 days).
- Contingency lanes: two parallel validation tracks (internal + vendor-run) to reduce blocker risk.
- Exec ask: dedicated 60-minute cutover readiness review with Acme engineering on 2026-09-24 (see Exec-ask-onepager.pdf).

Immediate asks from Acme: please confirm whether you can commit to the parallel validation lanes and whether the procurement sign-off can be completed by 2026-09-21. If procurement needs a formality or PO freeze, let us know and we will hold the canary rollout.

I'll leave Marissa and Rishi on this thread to handle the timelines and pricing impact; Grace is on standby for any compliance evidence you need.

Thanks,
Maya Srinivasan
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
maya@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: MAP-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), acceptance-gate-diagram.png (image), Exec-ask-onepager.pdf (pdf)

From: Jordan Miles <j.miles@acmehealth.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acmehealth.com>, Ava Collins <ava.collins@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acceptance gatebackfill and escalation: MAP v2 proposal

Maya — thanks for the clear doc. Quick responses from procurement/engineering after internal sync: 
- Procurement can complete formal sign-off by 2026-09-22 if we receive the final SOW and updated invoice today.
- Engineering is concerned about the parallel validation lanes — they can run the vendor lane but will only staff the internal lane at 50% capacity unless we compress scope.

Risk callout: if the internal validation is limited, we still run the chance of a late post-acceptance bug that requires a small rollback window. That would push final production by an additional 5–7 business days.

Can you produce a short scope-compressed checklist that allows the internal team to run at 80% effort? If so we can keep the acceptance window as proposed.

— Jordan
Jordan Miles
Head of Platform Delivery, Acme Health
j.miles@acmehealth.com

Date: Mon, 6 Sep 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acceptance gatebackfill and escalation: MAP v2 proposal

Jordan / team — appended below is the compressed validation checklist we can run to support an 80% internal staffing model. We will own the gating criteria for the vendor lane so your engineers can focus on core system tests.

Compressed acceptance checklist (high level):
1) Smoke: 6 core API flows validated (happy path only)
2) Regression: top 10 customer prompts validated end-to-end
3) Performance: 95th percentile latency within agreed SLA for 2k token runs
4) Security: SSO + audit log sanity check (Grace will produce the evidence pack)
5) Rollback plan: automated snapshot + 2-hour rollback window validated in staging

If Acme agrees to accept this reduced scope for the internal lane, we can commit to the parallel validation approach and keep the 2026-10-04 acceptance start.

Notes: this reduces coverage on deep edge cases; we recommend a followup 2-week stabilization sprint post-acceptance to catch residuals.

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Attachments: compressed-validation-checklist (sheet included in MAP-v2.xlsx)

From: Ava Collins <ava.collins@acmehealth.com>

Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acmehealth.com>, Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 14:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acceptance gatebackfill and escalation: MAP v2 proposal

Marissa / Maya — thanks, that checklist is helpful. Procurement will finalize SOW and invoice by morning 9/9; engineering confirms they can provide 80% staffing for the internal lane if Redwood owns the vendor lane and the rollback automation is staffed.

We accept the proposed acceptance window (2026-10-04 to 2026-10-11) under these conditions: 
- Redwood runs vendor validation and provides daily status updates (end-of-day).
- Exec readiness review on 2026-09-24 is confirmed; sending calendar invite.
- Procurement expects the final invoice line items for reserved capacity and support during the stabilization sprint.

Ava Collins
Director, Vendor Sourcing, Acme Health
ava.collins@acmehealth.com

Great — thank you, Ava. Quick recap and next steps (closing items):
- Procurement: final SOW/invoice expected 2026-09-09 (we received confirmation; thank you).
- Engineering: Acme commits 80% internal staffing; Redwood will operate the vendor validation lane and provide daily EOD reports.
- Exec readiness review: scheduled 2026-09-24, invite accepted.
- Acceptance window: 2026-10-04 to 2026-10-11 — confirmed.
- Contingency: if a post-acceptance rollback is required, we will use the 2-hour automated rollback; expected push to production will be up to +7 business days in the worst case (documented in MAP-v2.xlsx).

Action owners: 
- Marissa: lead vendor validation and daily status (start 2026-09-27)
- Rishi: finalize PO invoice lines and pricing addendum (deliver by 2026-09-09)
- Grace: compile compliance evidence pack for procurement (deliver by 2026-09-15)

I'll update the deal record with the new acceptance dates and attach MAP-v2. Please reply if any of the owners above should change.

Thanks everyone — closing the escalation ticket and marking the MAP as updated.
